12 Leonardo da Vinci proposed a flying machine that would work like a screw to lift the pilot into the
air. The ‘screw’ is rotated by the pilot.
The machine and the pilot together have a total mass of 120 kg.
Which useful output power must the pilot provide to move vertically upwards at a constant speed
of 2.5 m s–1?
A
48 W
B
300 W
C
470 W
D
2900 W

hints: Notice the motion is vertically upwards at constant speed of $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so the upward force must exactly balance the total weight of $120 \text{ kg}$.
Connect this to power for a force parallel to velocity, $P = Fv$, where $F$ here is the weight $mg$.
First calculate the weight $mg$ in $\text{N}$, then multiply by $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to get power in $\text{W}$ and compare with the four values.
walkthrough: Identify the useful given data: total mass $m = 120 \text{ kg}$ and constant upward velocity $v = 2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Because speed is constant, acceleration is zero, so the upward lifting force $F$ must equal the downward weight $W = mg$.
State the power rule for motion in the direction of the force: $P = Fv = mgv$.
Substitute with units: $P = 120 \text{ kg} \times 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2} \times 2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate the intermediate weight $mg \approx 1180 \text{ N}$ and then $P \approx 1180 \times 2.5 \approx 2940 \text{ W}$, which rounds to $2900 \text{ W}$.

A.explanation: This divides mass by speed, $120/2.5 = 48$, and ignores weight and the $P = Fv$ relationship.

B.explanation: This is $mv = 120 \times 2.5 = 300$, which uses mass instead of the lifting force equal to weight $mg$.

C.explanation: This is $mg/v \approx 471$, which divides the weight by speed instead of multiplying force by velocity.
